Usage: drive free <hold> <reason> ... [flags]

Hand back a hold that only a background job of its holder still keeps.

A hold frees itself once its holder's turn has ended and no background job
it started runs. Free hands it back sooner: the turn has ended, and the job
still running is not what the hold was taken for, such as an eval a release
step also started. The refusal on the hold prints the job's command; read
the holder's reply when the command does not say what the job is.

It is refused while the holder works, waits on a prompt, or its send is
under way; a hold nothing holds is reported free. A freed hold is free
until a send or open takes it again, so a step that uses it still names it
with --hold. It prints the step to run for each session that waits for the
hold.

Arguments:
  <hold>               The hold to free, as --hold named it, such as release.
  <reason> ...         What shows its holder no longer needs the hold; the log keeps it.

Inherited flags:
  -h, --help           Show context-sensitive help.
      --batch=NAME     Act in this batch, as drive prints its name, instead of the driver's current
                       one. It may stand anywhere on the line.
      --driver=NAME    Act in the batch this driver drives now; a chat driver's name is its
                       webhook's. It may stand anywhere on the line.

Examples:
  drive free release 'S2 released at 15:37; the job it left is its eval, which releases nothing'

Exit codes:
  0    success
  1    refused: nothing was done; next: says what to run instead
  2    invalid arguments; nothing was run
  3    tried and did not end as asked; the message says what did happen
  4    the session's login was rejected; next: relaunches it on another account, or says to tell the
       owner
